doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Leaving Shaw and joining Glenn Miller
summary: Notice from Shaw, advice from George Simon, and hiring by Miller at Glen Island Casino.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well tell me how your years with Glenn Miller came about.
Tell me how you got started with Glenn Miller. Was it 1939?

Yeah. Well I left the Shaw band in August 1939. There was something personal going on that I’d rather not talk about. But I was looking for a job. In other words, I got my notice from Shaw. I’m not afraid to say it. But it didn’t have anything to do with — well I can’t even say that.
Well he did suggest that I get a smaller bore horn. He thought my tone didn’t blend with Chuck Peterson and Bernie Privin. But there was more to this than I can talk about, involving another sex.
Sure, we can read between the lines on that.

Anyway, I was looking for a job, and we were at the hotel in Boston, I can’t remember, some plaza in Boston. So I came to New York on a day off. I talked to George Simon I guess. And I had called Benny Goodman and also Tommy Dorsey. No, I’m getting mixed up there at the end of the Miller thing, I’m sorry, that’s not right. But I did — Simon said, the Glen Island Casino was on the route between Boston and New York, and I was driving. So on the way back to Boston, Simon recommended I talk to Glenn Miller. So I did. And that’s where he hired me.
He just had three trumpets. And I the added trumpet. He had offered me a job about a year before that. And so I joined the band in Washington, D.C. at the Capitol Theater.
